structured_output.summary: The diff implements String.prototype.startsWith in the stub file, following the spec's 16 steps in order. RequireObjectCoercible, ToString(this), IsRegExp (with TypeError), ToString(searchString), and ToIntegerOrInfinity(position) are each called with ? and in the spec's order, so the observable operations match. The clamp to [0, length], the empty-search and end > length early returns, and the substring comparison all follow the spec. The string and search string are rooted across the user-observable conversions. No test-shaped branches, no swallowed errors, no made-up values. The gate reports build and clippy ok, and 34 new test262 passes with no regressions.
structured_output.notes_for_next_attempt: Nothing blocking. Minor points for the architect: (1) the NOTE comments and the header line from the stub were dropped; the ticket asks for steps as comments, so restoring them would be tidier. (2) The substring is taken as `agent.str(string)[start as usize..end as usize]`, which assumes the string storage is indexed in UTF-16 code units, matching str_len. The passing test262 runs suggest this is correct, but it is worth confirming that str() yields UTF-16 units and not a UTF-8 &str, since a byte-indexed &str would panic or misbehave on non-ASCII input.
